title: Orchestrator Review Load Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: A p5.js calculator for the daily review load of an agent team, L = fraction x n_p x k_p x r_p + n_e x k_e x r_e + c minutes, compared with the researcher's attention budget. Three challenges in a fixed order, two attempts each, ask for the load of the default team in hours, the largest number of planning agents that fits in 4 hours, and the largest fraction of planning outputs that can be reviewed. After each challenge the sim shows the worked calculation and a stacked bar of planning, execution, and conflict minutes against a dashed attention line, with the verdict in words. After the challenges, nine sliders unlock for exploration. All values are illustrative.

educational.topic: Researcher attention as the limit on the size of an agent team
learningObjectives: Calculate the daily review load of an agent team from its size and per-output review times, and adjust the team or the review fraction to fit a stated attention budget, in three challenges
prerequisites: the load formula L = n_p k_p r_p + n_e k_e r_e + c

canvasDimensions.controlHeight: 191 (3 slider columns, width >= 860 px) or 253 to 283 (2 slider columns)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description. The answer box (Enter submits), buttons, and nine sliders are native p5.js DOM controls reachable with the Tab key; each slider has an aria-label. Bar segments are labeled with their minutes and named in a legend, the attention limit is a dashed line with a text label, and fit or no-fit is stated in words with a check or X, so no meaning depends on color alone. All text is 13 px or larger.

controls.label: Answer
controls.purpose: Type the answer to the current challenge; Enter submits. A non-number is not counted as an attempt.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Checks the answer. Two attempts per challenge; a first miss shows a hint, a second miss shows the worked calculation and counts as missed.

controls.label: Next challenge / Start exploring
controls.purpose: Shown after a challenge ends. Moves to the next challenge, or after the third challenge opens exploration with the default values.

controls.label: Nine quantities: n_p, n_e, k_p, k_e, r_p, r_e, c, attention available, fraction of planning outputs reviewed
controls.purpose: Locked at the challenge values during the challenges (the unknown is hidden); unlocked in exploration, where each change updates the worked calculation and the bar.

controls.label: Restore defaults
controls.purpose: Exploration only. Returns all nine sliders to their default values.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate-then-decide: the learner computes the load by hand, receives the worked calculation and a visual comparison with the attention budget, then uses the formula to size the team or the review fraction
keyQuestions: How many hours of review does this team need each day?
How many planning agents fit in 4 hours of attention?
What fraction of planning outputs can be reviewed in 4 hours?
Which saves more attention: halving review time on planning outputs or on execution outputs?
commonMisconceptions: Review load grows only with the number of execution agents
More agents always means more done
Sampling review is the same as skipping review
assessmentOpportunities: Score on three challenges with two attempts each; mastery is 3 of 3 correct
Compare the saving from halving r_p with the saving from halving r_e
Find the largest team that fits a chosen attention budget
